workflow_stages: Where the assessment lives (standalone vs. embedded)

competitors.name: KnowBe4
competitors.entry_point: Content Manager (admin) for authoring/config; end-of-module Quiz or standalone SAPA (Security Awareness Proficiency Assessment) for learners
competitors.setup_friction: Content is vendor-authored; admin configures passing score and test-out toggle rather than writing questions
core_flow: Admin selects or configures training content in Content Manager
Learner completes inline Knowledge Checks during a module (immediate explanation shown)
Learner takes end-of-module Quiz or standalone SAPA to test retention
Score evaluated against configurable passing threshold (default 80%)
Failed learners can review questions and retake; some content allows test-out before starting training
feedback_states: inline explanation on Knowledge Check answers
competitors.error_prevention: Not documented at UI level in available sources
competitors.trust_model: Not documented; SAT training context, not simulation/agent trust framing
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Test-out toggle lets proficient users skip training entirely by passing the quiz upfront
competitors.risk_score_surface: absent (not found in reviewed sources; KnowBe4's model is not risk-score-adaptive per competitor-list.md)
competitors.source_notes: Based on indexed support-article summaries (ModStore/Library Guide, SAPA Overview, end-of-module quiz FAQ, KSAT Quiz Interactions Reports) returned via web search. Direct article fetches returned HTTP 403; exact UI mechanics are inferred from summaries, not observed directly.

competitors.name: Hoxhunt
competitors.entry_point: Micro-lesson quiz surfaced after a simulated phishing interaction, as part of an adaptive training path
competitors.setup_friction: Not admin-authored; content and triggering are Hoxhunt-curated/algorithmic
core_flow: User interacts with a simulated phishing test
Short micro-lesson with quiz is triggered
User completes quiz, earns stars/badges for engagement
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Adaptive training path personalizes future content, but not documented as an admin-facing efficiency tool
competitors.ai_personalization: observed (adaptive training path is a core positioning claim)
competitors.risk_score_surface: absent in reviewed quiz-specific sources (Hoxhunt has broader behavioral framing elsewhere per competitor-list.md)
competitors.remediation_path: observed at a high level (micro-lesson after a failed simulated interaction functions as remediation)
competitors.source_notes: Marketing and general support pages only; no documentation found on exact pass-score or retry mechanics for quizzes. 'No hard gating' is an inference from gamification framing, not a confirmed behavior.

competitors.name: Curricula (Huntress Managed SAT)
competitors.entry_point: Narrative training 'episodes' combining video, quiz, and phishing simulation
core_flow: Learner watches a story-driven training episode
Learner completes an interactive quiz tied to the episode
Quiz score tracked alongside completion rate and phishing report rate
feedback_states: not documented at a granular level
competitors.source_notes: Marketing pages and G2 summary only, post-acquisition rebrand from Curricula to Huntress Managed SAT; no UI walkthrough available.

observed_patterns: Inline Knowledge Check (teach) vs. end-of-content Quiz (test) as two distinct constructs (KnowBe4)
Test-out toggle letting proficient users skip training by passing the quiz first (KnowBe4)
Per-question interaction reporting for admins (KnowBe4 KSAT)
Gamified completion rewards in place of hard pass/fail gating (Hoxhunt)
Quiz bundled into a broader narrative/episode experience rather than exposed standalone (Curricula/Huntress)
anti_patterns: Soft/no pass-fail gating undercuts a compliance-oriented use case (Hoxhunt's gamification model)
Coupling quiz content to a full training episode removes the option for a lightweight standalone knowledge check (Curricula/Huntress)
differentiation_opportunities: Admin-facing bulk JSON question authoring is not offered by any of the three competitors reviewed — all are vendor-authored or algorithmically curated
Standalone assignability independent of any module is stronger than Curricula's bundled-episode model and cleaner than Hoxhunt's embedded-in-path approach
Per-user per-question answer drill-down already in Dune's designs matches KnowBe4's most advanced reporting (KSAT) and exceeds what Hoxhunt or Curricula document publicly
design_implications: Resolve whether Quiz teaches (show correct answer/explanation per question) or purely tests (no feedback until scored) before finalizing the end-user question flow
Keep the 80% default passing score — it matches industry expectation (KnowBe4) and needs no special justification
Treat JSON upload validation and error states as a first-class design surface since bulk authoring is Dune's clearest differentiator here and its clearest risk
Keep passing-score/retake as a hard gate; do not soften toward Hoxhunt's engagement-only model, which fits a different positioning
confidence_notes: KnowBe4: medium confidence, sourced from indexed support-article summaries; direct fetches were blocked (HTTP 403), so exact UI mechanics are inferred from summaries
Hoxhunt: low confidence, marketing/support pages only, no documented pass-score or retry mechanics
Curricula/Huntress: low-to-medium confidence, marketing and G2 summary only, no UI walkthrough available, post-acquisition rebrand may have stale legacy documentation
